verdicts.reason: Confirmed partial (high). Metadata: Crossref and INSPIRE agree: D. Mukherjee, H. K. Jassal, K. Lochan, Eur. Phys. J. C 84 (2024) 318 (issue 3, online 2024-03-26), doi:10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12673-1; arXiv 2022, read as v4 (27 Mar 2024). Why partial: the abstract and sec. 8 state, for the present epoch, that 'the effect of dark energy can alternatively be realized as collapse of space in a conformally connected universe, at least classically'. Sec. 6 pairs a de Sitter Jordan frame with a contracting Einstein frame whose only content is a massless scalar (stiff, V = 0). That is C5's identity and the shape of its route, in another duality, and it meets the standard the check already applied to the pre-big-bang pairing (hep-th/0207130, partial). Not anticipation: the partner is a Weyl-rescaled metric chosen with a free parameter, not the momentum-space description, and dark energy stays Λ or quintessence, put in by hand. Corrections to the finding. (1) The body is weaker than the abstract. The Jordan frame collapses only while 1 + w_φ of the Einstein-frame content exceeds a threshold set by the chosen Brans-Dicke parameter (eqs. 26, 37-38), and a pure Λ never meets it. For ΛCDM 'the Jordan frame universe is seen to be collapsing at the early matter-dominated phase' and then bounces, so the Λ-dominated future always maps to an expanding Jordan frame. The freezing example likewise collapses before today and expands after. In the main construction (secs. 3-5) the content that drives the collapse sits on the expanding side, the reverse of C5's route; only sec. 6 has C5's orientation. Collapse during Einstein-frame acceleration needs w_BD < -1 in the flat case (checks.py E). The thawing example reaches it by choosing w_BD ≈ -1.45 (ϖ₀ = 0.105, q₀ = -0.445; checks.py C). The authors themselves say the Jordan phases 'need not be corresponding to certain eras in the Einstein frame'. (2) Drop the clause that sec. 5.2 'bears on the open question of how the route relates to τ's potential'. Λ⁴(1 + cos(φ/f)) is the standard PNGB thawing potential, cited from Chiba-De Felice-Tsujikawa 2013 [49] and Amendola-Tsujikawa [23]. In that example the potential-dominated field is on the expanding side and its thawing triggers the collapse. Nothing there maps dual kinetic energy to Λ, and the shared form is generic. (3) Sec. 6 is a textbook Brans-Dicke vacuum solution (w_BD = -4/3, cited to Faraoni 2004 [1]), and the paper does not cite the pre-big-bang literature. The conformal pairing of a stiff collapse with an accelerated expansion is Gasperini-Veneziano's (already on known.json), so sec. 6 adds its de Sitter, late-time instance, not a new pairing. (4) In sec. 6, ã ∝ a^(-1/2) at the same event (eqs. 9a, 46; checks.py A), and the two frames run on different clocks (dt̃ = Ω dt). The program has a·ã = 1 and one shared lapse. Eq. 47's prefactor carries a₀^(3/2) where eqs. 9a and 46 give a₀; the two agree for a₀ = 1, and the difference is immaterial. Also confirmed: the paper is in g4 verify.json new_findings and absent from round3/known.json (0 matches).

verdicts.reason: Downgraded to related (high). Metadata: Crossref and INSPIRE agree: D. Mukherjee, H. K. Jassal, K. Lochan, JCAP 2021, issue 12, article 016 (online 2021-12-06), doi:10.1088/1475-7516/2021/12/016. The paper states an expansion-collapse duality between a quintessence Einstein frame and its f(R) Jordan dual, as an 'equivalent description'. It never says that the collapse is, or accompanies, the acceleration, and its own condition rules that pairing out. The Jordan frame collapses if and only if w_φ > 6H̃²/(κ²ρ_φ) - 1 = 2/Ω_φ - 1 (eq. 68), so collapse during Einstein-frame acceleration needs Ω_φ > 3, that is Ω_K < -2 (checks.py E). In its examples the collapse begins where the quintessence reaches w = 1 ('the Jordan frame scale factor has a maximum value at the critical point', w(ã) = 1, at ã = 49.2). With dust and positive curvature it begins at ã ≈ 20.5, where w_φ ≈ 0.58. Both are decelerating Einstein frames (checks.py B). With dust at the observed ratio 'the Jordan frame universe never collapses' (sec. 5). The abstract says the Einstein frame 'continues to expand', not that it accelerates. The paper shares C5's theme, a dark-energy universe with a dual that collapses while ours expands, but states neither the collapse-acceleration identity nor a stiff-to-Λ pairing; its stiff content sits on the expanding side. The finding's own difference ('does not yet say that the collapse is the effect of dark energy') already points this way.

INSPIRE agrees (recid 2627610, cnum C21-07-05.3, no arXiv eprint), and an arXiv author search (Mukherjee and Lochan) finds only 2105.10521 and 2207.02835. OpenAlex wrongly names the container 'The Ninth Marcel Grossmann Meeting'. The MG16 Indico page (contribution 454, 9 July 2021) lists the talk under the JCAP 2021 title and abstract. The proceedings abstract classifies 'quintessence models in the Einstein frame that are dual to f(R) gravity theories in the Jordan frame', so the f(R) collapse condition of 2105.10521 applies: collapse during Einstein-frame acceleration is possible only for Ω_K < -2. The abstract states the duality and 'an effective description of a collapsing universe in terms of an expanding one', the reverse direction, and says nothing about dark energy or acceleration. It adds no content to JCAP 2021. As proceedings it would count only by stating the conjecture itself, which its abstract does not.
